newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: COSTA RICAN PINEAPPLE EXPORTS SEEN RISING.
newsitem.headline: COSTA RICAN PINEAPPLE EXPORTS SEEN RISING.

text.p: Costa Rica pineapple output should continue grow this year for an expected trade worth $75 million, compared with $69 million a year ago, an industry businessman said.

"We are in the process of increasing production and expect to boost it by 800,000 (40-kg) boxes each year for the next three years," Rodrigo Jimenez, the general director of lead producing and exporting company Pindeco, told Reuters.
Pindeco is a division of Del Monte Fresh Produce and exports between 70 and 75 percent of Costa Rica's pineapple.

Jimenez said the company plans to develop 500 hectares of new plantations, adding a new variety of pineapple called "Del Monte Gold." He said the new pineapple variety has a brighter yellow color, a higher sugar content and more Vitamin C than other varieties.
"All these characteristics have translated to a greater demand in the United States and Europe, which is why we expect an increase in exports," Jimenez said.
The company expects to produce about 5.6 million 40-kg boxes in Costa Rica this year, he added.
